AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Balanced Meal? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Balanced Meal.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Balanced Meal.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Balanced Meal.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Balanced Meal.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Fruits.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Fruits.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Fruits.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Fruits.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Personal Hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Personal Hygiene.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Personal Hygiene.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Personal Hygiene.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Personal Hygiene.

11. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Making Tacking Stitches? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Making Tacking Stitches.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Making Tacking Stitches.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Making Tacking Stitches.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Making Tacking Stitches.

13. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

14. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

15. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Wild Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Wild Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Wild Animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Wild Animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Wild Animals.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Making Tacking Stitches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Fuel Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Wild Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Growing Fruits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
